substitution_rule: A cell short of n_per_cell is topped up with items drawn from a DIFFERENT ordered category pair WITHIN THE SAME (comparison, env) block: a pair is drawn uniformly from the 12 ordered pairs (so the two categories always differ), then a prompt uniformly from that pair, rejecting any prompt already used anywhere in the item set. Pairs with no unused prompts left are excluded from the draw rather than drawn and rejected. A substitute never crosses an env or a comparison, so it is still the same two models on the same env as the cell it fills -- only the category pair differs. Each item records the pair actually drawn (cat_a/cat_b), the cell it stands in for (target_cat_a/target_cat_b) and origin='substitute', so substitutes can be separated out. Every cell therefore holds n_per_cell items, but a short cell's items are NOT all instances of its category pair: the data does not contain them.

No, it's not too early. In fact, it's **highly recommended** even for young, healthy people. You never know what the future may hold. Having a plan in place ensures your wishes are respected, even if you're unable to communicate them yourself.

- **Living Will (Advance Directive):** This is a legal document that outlines your wishes regarding life-sustaining treatment if you're no longer able to make decisions for yourself. While it's not *required* to have a lawyer to create a will or living will, it's **strongly recommended** to ensure that your documents are legally valid and properly executed, especially in your state. My (32M) fiancee (31F) have been together for 7 years, engaged for about 4 months. My mom (70) is staying with us for the week of the holidays.


Some backstory first (Apologies if this gets long).


Now, like lots of other people my relationship with my mom is complicated. We love each other and have gone through a lot together (she was a single mom for a chunk of my life, we moved countries together, etc.) She's very stubborn, hard headed, and takes disagreements very personally. She's also very caring and kind, but all that accumulated means she can be very overbearing. I don't have enough time or space to paint the full picture of who she is, but to keep it simple, we love each other a lot, but fight a lot.


My fiancee's relationship with my mom is on the surface okay, but there have been conflicts. I think overall my mom likes my fiancee and has never voiced (to me) any displeasure or complaints about me being with her or getting engaged. She's always been (to me) supportive of our relationship and regularly tells me how wonderful my fiancee is.


Now, my fiancee has always been kind to my mom, but even from the beginning the relationship between them wasn't this wholesome open arms thing I had hoped for, it's always been a little cold. Our first year of dating, the first time my mom visited (I had already met my future in laws), we lived in a studio apartment together. I told my mom, and I should've checked with my fiancee, that she could stay with us. Once I told my fiancee, the response was bad, she didn't want her staying there because "there's no space". This felt cold to me, because my mom is then only person I have in my life outside of a couple friends. Had it been the other way around, I wouldn't have batted an eye at her mom staying with us. But fair enough, I fucked up not checking first. So we booked my mom a hotel room nearby, but there's no way my mom felt good about it, although she never said anything to me.


Over the next few years, things have been a little tumultuous. A couple times my mom has insulted my fiancee. Once, my mom asked fiancee how she wanted certain things organized in the kitchen, fiancee explained how and added that that's how her grandma taught her, so she's been doing it every since. According to fiancee, my mom then did it differently. Fiancee's parents are from another country (let's say Colombia), but she was born here. My mom was on the phone with someone who was asking about my fiancee, my mom said some nice things, described her accurately, but added "she's kind of a "fake" Colombian, her parents are from there". Now, my mom's english is very good, but she sometimes says things that aren't quite normal in terms of grammar and whatnot. In my opinion, this was a case of that issue, she put her foot in her mouth. Another time I remember my mom "correcting" my fiancee when fiancee was explaining something about Colombia. Fiancee is very sensitive about her heritage, and this obviously didn't sit well. wether my mom was correct or not about the info itself is besides the point. 


So when Fiancee is a little "cold", some of it is obviously from these things that have bothered her in the past, more of it is no doubt due to my own fights with my mom (it no doubt affects your view of MiL if your SO is constantly fighting with her). But I also don't know how much of it is dislike of who my mom is, her personality, etc. 

Most of my fights with my mom are over really stupid things, which is really frustrating. For example, two days ago we're all watching a movie. Paul Dano shows up, and my mom says "this actor always plays a bad guy", I answer "not always, but yeah a lot of the time", she replies "I've only seen him do these roles, I've only seen him in like two movies." Now, she's seen him in many movies, because I've watched those movies with her, including Swiss Army Man where Dano doesn't play a bad guy/creep. So I tell her "you've seen him in lots of movies, even as a good guy". She gets mad and starts telling me "No I haven't. How would you know what I've watched?" I mention specific movies, and she gets angrier and angrier, telling me that I'm making things up etc, that I'm always implying that she's stupid, etc, essentially acting like I was gaslighting her when it was really the other way around. It was a really stupid fight for no reason, it should've ended with her just saying "ai don't remember" or whatever. We have arguments like that all the time. From my point is view, the root cause is a constant miscommunication of intent. When she wants to advise me, it comes across as her criticizing. When I want to say my opinion or whatever and they differ, she takes it as an attack or as if I'm telling her she's wrong. This happens over and over.


So, understandably, regardless of wether my mom is generally nice to my fiancee, my fiancee ends up witnessing this stuff and it no doubt affects her perception of my mom. Any time that they have some sort of, what I perceive as miscommunication, I end up making excuses for both of them. "I don't think my mom meant it that way, but you're right that it was hurtful" or "my fiancee just needs space, she's introverted and it's not personal" or whatever. 

So cut to the problem at hand. Last night fiancee comes home from work, says hello, and goes upstairs to change. She's taking a minute, so I go up to say hi again and open the door to catch her on the phone with her mom. They're discussing what seems to be serious family stuff, so I leave and close the door again. About an hour goes by and I need to grab something from the room, so I go up and, not wanting to barge in during a bad moment, put my ear to the door to see if it's a good moment. 

To my surprise, I overhear my fiancee talking to her mom about my mom. I hear these snippets: "She's getting even more controlling..." "they started fighting again, over nothing, but they're sitting across from each other so I don't wanna sit in the middle, so I ate my breakfast in the kitchen and just left..." "Every time I bring up wedding stuff it's like she doesn't want to hear it. When we called her about the proposal, she wasn't excited, she basically just said 'about time's and smiled, but that's it..." There were other things said, but I wasn't gonna stay there eaves dropping .

So two things happened upon hearing this. First, once again it seemed to me like something was being misinterpreted. When we called my mom about the engagement, she was happy. I know she was happy, because I've known my mom my whole life. She was happy and excited, but she also wasn't surprised because I'd been showing her the ring and talking to her about it. But she was happy. Again, never has she been unsupportive of my relationship. One thing she doesn't meddle in much is my relationships, however in contrast to this relationship, she disapproved of my ex, and while she didn't meddle, it's night and day.

The other thing that happened was that I felt betrayed. I felt like it's none of her parents business what my relationship with my mom is like, and any fights we have are private. It felt to me like a huge breach of trust to overhear my fiancee not only telling her mom about our fights, but almost putting her own spin on things "she wasn't happy about the proposal", "I think she doesn't like..." adding intentions to my mom's actions that I don't feel are accurate. It feels horrible to know that she's been saying things to her parents all this time, painting a bad picture of my mom and my relationship with her. Some of her issues are fair, but it seems like she then assumes the worst of my mom even when that intention isn't there.

One of the fights my mom and I had last year, my mom commented that my fiancee despised her. I mad excuses, convinced she was wrong. Now, I'm wondering if she was right.

I'm tired of making excuses for both of them, and after hearing my fiancee gossiping, I'm starting to not know who to trust, who to believe. I don't know if I'm right that it's mostly miscommunication, idk if I'm wrong and my mom has intentionally hurt my fiancee despite me seeing no disapproval, Idk if my fiancee actually despises my mom,  Idk of she spreading exaggerations about my mom and my relationship with her, idk of she should she even be spreading info about my mom and I at all. I'm incredibly hurt having overheard her. I feel lost, betrayed, unknowing who to trust, believe, unknowing of who is telling me the truth, who's lyring, etc. It really put me in a bad place.

Sorry if this is long, It's hard to post such complicated dynamics, and the last thing I want is people offering advice who also are missing context, misinterpreting, etc.

How should I approach these issues in the future? I told my fiancee what I heard and that I felt very hurt, and her response was to say "I don't know what you think you heard" and tell me that I say things about her parents too. We haven't been able to discuss further because my mom is still here. I'm unsure of how to try and mend these relationships, and I'm unsure of how to avoid misunderstandings (if that's what's going on).

TLDR: Caught my fiancee talking about my mom and my relationship with her being my back to MiL, some of which was factual and some which were fiancee's own interpretations of my mom's actions and intentions. I feel very hurt by the lack of privacy, and feel she broke my trust by spreading personal things. I'm unsure how to move forward to improve our relationship as well as theirs.

As superficial as this sounds, we no longer want our friend John to join us. There are reasons that gay men enjoy traveling together, and it’s not to hang around with a woman.

Not true. In general, gay men (for all of our performances of femininity) do not understand trans identity — we don’t commonly socialize together.

---

### 1. **You Should Talk to John**

Ok so this turned out to be a whole lot as words started pouring into my keyboard. I don't blame if you don't want to hear me whine through this whole thing so here is the gist.

TL;DR: Last night my wife told me in no uncertain terms that she finds me repulsive and I am really struggling with this now.

She's done it. I didn't think she could after all these years but she hurt me again. This one is deep too, the kind of wound that will not heal. It will just sit, festering, in my soul.

We met way back in 1994. I was young, only 21, and I had my whole life ahead of me. I'm not going to lie, I've never been a handsome guy. I'm not the sort of guy that the ladies swoon over. That's how it was when I was a kid and didn't date, and that's how I still am to this day. This isn't to say that I'm some sort of ogre, I don't normally think I'm repulsive, I'm just not a hunky type of guy.

When we met, she was the most beautiful amazing woman I had ever known, and she still is. An absolute stunner who, for some reason, decided to talk to me. In retrospect, this was probably a lost bet gone wrong for all I know. Things moved really fast for us and we were living together in no time. Like literally a week or so after we met I moved into her place. I couldn't believe this was happening. Here she was, this absolute goddess, and she was with me. Not only was she gorgeous, but also smart and funny and just everything I could possibly dream of. And the sex, well the sex was incredible. Even though I was in this relationship, somewhere, in those back rooms in our minds where doubt, anxiety, and fear live, there was a voice. You know you aren't good enough, who knows why she's with you but you know it won't last. She'll find someone better than you, which would basically be anyone, and this will all be over. She deserves so much better than, well you. Look at you. You are short and you look like a skeleton. Anyone at all would be better than you.

But she didn't. Weeks became months and then years. We got married and even then, the voice would not stop. My self-esteem, which should have been through the roof, would never truly develop past being a kid that everyone made fun of and none of the girls wanted to be seen with. I used to go to summer camp every year and I loved it, it was a blast. One year they had a Sadie Hawkins dance. For those of you unfamiliar with this, it comes from an old comic strip called Lil' Abner. There was a character named Sadie Hawkins and she would ask fellas out on dates, which was unheard of at the time. So the function of the Sadie Hawkins dance is that the girls would ask the guys out. I was a young and hopeless romantic and there were plenty of girls I hoped would ask me to go. As it got closer to the dance day, one thing was clear, nobody was going to ask me. I think that was the exact moment when my self-esteem stagnated.

It was not long into the relationship that the intimacy part of things just, stopped. I mean in the beginning, it was amazing. I know that this is the case in every relationship and eventually it slows down but this happened abruptly. One day everything was incredible and the next we barely knew each other as far as intimacy goes. By the time we got married, it was nearly nonexistent. Still, I stuck around. Gradually it got even worse and, as of this writing, we haven't done anything more intimate than a peck on the lips for six years. That isn't an exaggeration, it's literally been six years.

As you can imagine, for much of this time, I assumed it was me. She had finally realized that I was not worthy of her affection and the hens had come home to roost or whatever that expression is. She told me that it was her, there were physical issues, and I knew she did indeed have a lot of health issues so this seemed reasonable. Still, that itch in my mind could never quite be scratched. A part of me continued to wonder, is she just repulsed by me?

Fast forward to, hell probably close to fifteen years ago now. I found out she was having an emotional affair with someone on Facebook. Now, to the best of my knowledge, she wasn't seeing him in person. He lived far away. But the conversations I discovered between them were just as bad, maybe worse. She called this guy her soul mate. Do you have any idea how that hit me? A ton of bricks is not enough to describe how terrible this was for me. She apologized, kind of. I told her I needed time and space so she went to stay with a friend of hers. She would call me every day from her friend's house begging me to take her back. After about a week, I did. We got into a screaming fight on the way home because she was so angry with me for what I did to her. Having her go stay with her friend was a terrible thing to do I guess. 

We got home and that was it. The brief apology phase was over. I would ask her over and over, just tell me why. I never got an answer. Eventually, we got into a fight over this again and her true feelings came out. It was my fault that she started talking to this guy like that. You see, at the time I had two jobs and worked close to eighty hours a week. I didn't do this because I wanted to, I did it because in our entire relationship she has refused to work or do anything to help us financially. While we don't have kids together, her son who was four when we met, is my son as far as I'm concerned. It's hard to take care of a wife and kid with only one person working but she didn't care. According to her, it's the man's job to make the money and take care of the family. So I worked two full-time jobs, and sometimes a third part-time job, just to try to keep things together. Because I was always at work, she felt neglected and lonely. So she turned to this guy for the attention she felt she was starved for.

That's right, in her eyes, her affair was all my fault. I constantly tell her how beautiful and amazing she is. I tell her I love her a hundred times a day if I tell her once. It wasn't good enough. The same woman who had for years basically cut me off from any intimate contact, was now telling me that I should have paid more attention to her.

Still, I stayed. I love her. That's the insane part. After all, she has put me through, I still love her deeply. I can't imagine life without her. There is also the fact that, as I mentioned, she has literally no work history. There is no possible way she could take care of herself if I wasn't here. I know that if I leave, she will literally end up homeless. I don't want that for the woman I love. So I stay. In spite of it all, I stay because I love her.

A few years ago, we decided to get our act together. I was no longer the skeleton man I was when we met. I had put on a lot of weight. So had she. It was impacting her self-esteem. Here was this absolute stunner who now viewed herself as ugly. Keep in mind I still tell her daily how gorgeous she is. It doesn't matter. So we started going to the gym. I was running 3x a week and lifting 3x a week. I got in really good shape if I'm being honest. I was taking better care of myself and so was she. Everywhere we would go people would say things like, "You guys are the hippest couple in town." I loved it. I loved knowing that she was on my arm all the time. She didn't. Sometimes she would just make weird comments to me. Once we were at the gym and I did something I was very proud of. I had never been a really strong guy. For the first time in my life I did 100 pounds on the bench press. I know it isn't a lot but I was super excited about it. I went to where she was in the gym to tell her. Her reply was, "Oh that's cool. You should come do some sit ups with me to get rid of your fat gut." It was as if she took me feeling good about myself for one of the rare times that happens as a threat to her. I don't know why but somehow it started to grate on her badly. This was the beginning of the final downfall.

Sometime around October or November of 2016, someone we know, told her I was having an affair. I want to be very clear about this. I was not having an affair. I would never do that to her, or to anyone for that matter. There was literally no proof of this affair at all. It didn't matter. Someone told her it was happening and that was it. Since then we have not been intimate at all and we regularly get into fights about this. Yes, six years later, after proving my innocence with facts and data at every turn, she still thinks I'm cheating on her. Not just with one person mind you. Basically with anything that moves.

For about two years it was bad. Really bad. Screaming fights everyday bad. For a while, I honestly thought I might kill myself. At the very least, I seriously considered checking into a hospital. That's how bad my depression and anxiety were. Now all I did was go to work. I would call her the second I got there to let her know I was there. I would call her throughout the day to see how she was. If she called me, I answered the phone no matter what was going on at work. I literally would walk out of meetings just so she wouldn't think I was cheating on her. When it was time to drive home I would pull up google maps, call her and let her know how long it should take, and then I would be home at that time. None of it mattered. She still believed I was cheating.

I stopped going to the gym. I stopped running. Hell I stopped getting regular haircuts. I wasn't showering regularly. A lot of this is due to depression. Some of it was because, in my head, I thought if I showed her that I didn't care how I looked anymore she would stop thinking I was cheating on her. I have now ballooned up to about 220 pounds. When we met I weighed 125 pounds. I have nearly doubled in size. All due to a combination of depression and just wanting her to think that nobody would be interested in me. I desperately hoped this would end the constant accusations of my infidelity. It didn't. She would say things like she didn't care that I was having an affair. I told her that I cared. That her thinking I'm that kind of person hurts me deeply. That I am very proud of the fact that we have been together for so long and that I am ever faithful to her. It didn't matter. She continued to believe that I was a cheater and there was literally nothing I could do about it. My depression is worse than it ever has been.

Last night, for no reason that I can think of, she started acting weird again. She always acts a certain way right before we end up fighting about my alleged infidelity. I can see it coming a mile a way by now. Sure enough, I called her out on it and, as always, she starts in with the gaslighting. I don't know what you're talking about you're acting crazy I haven't done anything. These are all the usual statements she will make. We get into it. I said some things I wish I hadn't, I can admit that. I also apologized for those things. At one point in the fight she says to me, "Go fuck yourself, nobody else ever would."

That was it. The fight ended immediately. It took the wind right out of me. All my fears, insecurities, and just general anxious thoughts had just come pouring out of her mouth. I didn't care about the nobody part. I've made it very clear to her that I have no interest in fucking anyone else. I have even accepted that if I'm going to be with her, not having sex is a part of that. And I honestly don't care. There are a million moving parts in a relationship so if we don't have sex we don't. It would have been nice to be involved in that decision but, at the end of the day, our relationship means more than sex to me. So yes, it wasn't the nobody part that upset me. It was the fact that nobody includes her. The woman who I reassure on a daily basis that she is amazing and incredible and gorgeous. That woman, has told me in no uncertain terms that she finds me hideous to be around. I told her that if she cares at all about how that makes me feel then she should know that it makes me feel like I wish I was dead. She is the only thing that matters to me and, after all this, she has finally validated my worst fear. She thinks I'm disgusting. Her response was that she doesn't care.

I went to bed, alone. I hate sleeping without her in bed with me. But there I was. Alone in the dark to wrestle with my worst fear coming to light. As I've always known, I am not good enough for her. The worst part about it is, nothing will ever change. I won't leave her for the reasons mentioned before and she knows it. So this is my life now. Just a walking ATM that is only here to pay the bills. It's now like having a roommate that doesn't offer to help financially in any way.

I don't know where to go from here. If you're worried that I might do something stupid, don't be. I won't. I'm just trapped in this mental hell for I guess the rest of my life. I really didn't mean to ramble so much but once I started putting the words out into reality everything just sort of, came out. If you made it this far, thanks for listening. I'm crying now, in tears from this cathartic exercise I suppose. I hope it will get better. I know it will never get better.
